messages:
alyssa: Quick heads-up — after landing the fp8 calibration change last night I see a weird latency pattern on long-context runs. TPS is fine but first-token latency (startup TTFT) for 8k+ contexts jumped ~2.4x on the INT8/FP8 mixed builds.

marc: ugh. do you have traces or a short repro?

alyssa: yes. running the long-story benchmark (8k prompt + 512 decode) on a 4-GPU shard. Repro steps and a trimmed perf dump below. It's most visible when we switch kernel variants mid-request (initial encode path vs streaming decode path).

alyssa: ```
# simplified nvprof counters (avg over 10 runs)
baseline (fp8 calibr v1): total_tokens=8200, TPS=420, startup_ttft=18ms
after calib v2: total_tokens=8200, TPS=410, startup_ttft=44ms
kernel hotlist:
  prefill_gemm_fp8_fast   48%
  decode_gemm_int8_stream 30%
  kv_cache_write          12%
  kv_cache_read           7%
note: we see repeated small KV evictions around token 1-4 of the decode phase.
```

sam: interesting — so throughput (TPS) roughly stable but TTFT jumps, which smells like a scheduling or kernel switch penalty. Could be queue flush + KV reformat cost when we pick the streaming INT8 kernels.

ravi: any chance calibration v2 changed per-layer quant params that force a different kernel path for the first decode microbatch? like we pick prefill-optimized kernels for the encode, then immediately pick decode-optimized kernels that have higher warmup.

alyssa: exactly. calibration v2 chooses different per-layer thresholds, so the runtime toggles from the "fast prefill" fp8 kernels to a different int8/4bit decode kernel combo. That kernel combo has worse small-batch startup perf (higher TTFT) even though steady-state is similar. The extra cost shows up on long-context because the switch happens after the big KV write and before streaming.

marc: can you paste the kernel selection log snippet?

alyssa: ```
[kernel-select] layer=0 prefill->kernel=fp8_prefill_fast (batch=32)
[kernel-select] layer=0 decode->kernel=int8_stream_v3 (microbatch=1)
[kv] kv_write shards=4 size=18MB latency=12ms
[kv] kv_read  shards=4 size=1.2MB latency=3ms
[scheduler] microbatch flush at decode-start: 9ms
```

jen: hmm — kernel churn + microbatch flush + a synchronous KV flush looks like the triad. My gut: two mitigations: 1) add hysteresis so we don't switch kernel families within the same logical request, or 2) pre-warm the decode kernel path during the tail of prefill so the decode kernel's device state + memory layouts are ready.

sam: agree. We also saw before that some int8 kernels have a high init latency due to different workspace allocation sizes. If the runtime frees and re-allocs scratch buffers between prefill and decode, that'll add a few ms.

ravi: another angle — batching heuristics. For long contexts we currently let the scheduler drain prefill batches fully before starting streaming decode microbatches. If we instead overlap the last prefill batch with the first decode microbatch (overlap the KV write with the decode kernel warming), we might hide some of the TTFT cost. But that risks KV consistency unless we ensure read-after-write ordering.

alyssa: tried a quick patch locally: warmed the decode kernel asynchronously on token -2 and pinned the decode kernel variant for the whole request. Result: startup TTFT dropped to 20ms (near baseline) and TPS unchanged. Side effect: +1MB pinned scratch allocator for duration of request.

marc: good data. What's the regression risk? If we pin kernel family for the whole request, we might lose some steady-state perf on mixed workloads (where decode kernels are faster on average).

alyssa: true. For our workload the steady-state delta is <3% TPS. But pinning avoids the 2x TTFT regression on long-contexts. Option: only pin when context_length > threshold or when calibration indicates a kernel-family flip.

jen: we should also consider a lighter-weight heuristic: prefer kernel_variant_by_phase with warmup flags — runtime picks decode kernels but queues a 1-shot warmup call on the device asynchronously before the microbatch loop. That doesn't require pinning and keeps flexibility.

ravi: also worth adding a perf counter to detect kernel-switch-induced TTFT spikes so we can auto-roll back per-customer. Perf-bot can create alerts if TTFT > baseline*1.8 for 5 runs.

perf-bot: Alert rule created: channel=eng-runtime, metric=first_token_latency, threshold=1.8x baseline, lookback=5 runs.

sam: sounds like immediate short-term plan: (A) add async decode kernel warmup on last prefill batch, (B) add hysteresis threshold to kernel selector, (C) instrument and alert. Medium term: revisit per-layer calibration to reduce family flips.

marc: +1. Can you open a tiny RFC / PR with the warmup patch and include your perf dumps? I'll review and we can try a canary on dedicated cluster.

alyssa: on it — will put up a PR later today with reproducer, nvprof snippet, and the warmup change. tagging @marc for review and @perf-bot for canary alerts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
